key: Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them: Ye shall be holy; for I the LORD your God am holy.
s: Heading a chapter of laws on worship, justice and neighbourly love, the LORD addresses the whole congregation through Moses; Rashi, on 19:2, reads the call to holiness as keeping apart from forbidden unions and from sin, and Ramban, on 19:2, as restraint even in what the Torah permits, lest one become a scoundrel within its licence.

evidence.gloss: [Rashi on 19:2, ‘Ye shall be holy’:] Be separate from forbidden unions and from transgression, for wherever you find a fence against unchastity you find holiness. [Ramban on 19:2:] In my view this separateness is not separating from forbidden unions, as the Rabbi says, but the separateness named throughout the Talmud, whose practitioners are called Perushim … and so he would be a scoundrel with the Torah’s permission … and He commanded a general matter, that we be separate from what is permitted.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok; ref Leviticus 19:2 and at [108,2] match). Plain sense faithful: 19:1 to 2 open the chapter with the LORD telling Moses to speak to all the congregation, and the chapter goes on to worship, justice and love of the neighbour (19:18). Opened the whole 19:2 packet. Rashi on קדשים תהיו: separate from forbidden unions and from transgression. Ramban on the same lemma quotes Rashi, says in his own words that the separateness is not that of forbidden unions ‘as the Rabbi says’, but restraint in permitted things, lest a man be a scoundrel with the Torah’s permission. Genuine difference, named by Ramban himself and not resolved in the sentence (rule 5). The only sexual reference is Rashi’s own non-graphic term.
